'''Barry Paw''' was a [[Burmese American]] [[biologist]]. He was notable for his role in discovering a new gene in humans that contributes to the production of [[hemoglobin]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-03-05 |title=Burmese Researcher Helps Discover New Gene |url=https://burmese.voanews.com/a/a-27-2006-03-05-voa5-93508799/1231960.html |access-date=2023-05-22 |website=ဗွီအိုအေ |language=my |archive-date=2023-05-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230522162944/https://burmese.voanews.com/a/a-27-2006-03-05-voa5-93508799/1231960.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Paw worked in the [[United States]] as a researcher at [[Harvard Medical School]] and had undertaken research into how the gene [[Mitoferrin-1|mitoferrin]] transports iron to [[red blood cells]] to form hemoglobin.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hms.harvard.edu/dms/BBS/fac/paw.php |title=Barry H. Paw |year=2012 |work=Biological and Biomedical Sciences |publisher=Harvard College |accessdate=8 April 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140624224223/http://www.hms.harvard.edu/dms/bbs/fac/Paw.php |archivedate=24 June 2014 }}</ref> Hemoglobin carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body, including the muscles.

Paw's research was targeted to reveal changes in the genes that cause human diseases, including [[iron deficiency]] or those which cause an excessive amount of iron. His research team pioneered the use of zebrafish to model anaemia-causing mutations and more. For example, they were able to identify the molecular basis of Tay-Sachs disease.

Dr. Paw died unexpectedly on December 28, 2017, at the age of 55.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaplan |first=Jerry |date=January 3, 2018 |title=In Memoriam In Memory of Barry Paw |url=https://bioiron.org/news/in-memoriam/in-memory-of-barry-paw.aspx |access-date=May 14, 2024 |website=International Society for the Study of Iron in Biology and Medicine |archive-date=May 14, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240514193812/https://bioiron.org/news/in-memoriam/in-memory-of-barry-paw.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref>
